one_line: Hands-on first look at Cursor's new terminal agent CLI (beta) using GPT-5: install, slash commands, a Kanban app test, and why the host would not switch from Claude Code yet.
summary: The host frames Cursor's new terminal agent as a competitive response to Claude Code, with GPT-5 as its main model and model switching as its main advantage. He walks through installing the CLI from Cursor's site, logging in through the browser, and the beta warning about security risks. He lists missing features: Cursor rules and ignore files (such as ignoring .env) are not implemented, files cannot be referenced, and images cannot be dragged in. The built-in slash commands are /model, an auto-run mode, duplicate new-chat and clear commands, and Vim mode, which Claude Code already has. In his test, a prompt to build a Kanban app in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with a liquid-glass style hung for about 8 minutes, and a second identical run worked. The output had a header overlap bug and a card-shape bug on drag; a follow-up prompt fixed the card shape but not the overlap, and an image placed in the project folder did not appear to be read. He concludes the agent is too limited to justify leaving Claude Code, and that Cursor gives up its IDE advantage by moving to a terminal.

key_ideas.idea: Cursor's new agent is a terminal CLI, positioned against Claude Code; its main differentiator is that it can switch models, and it uses GPT-5 in the test.
key_ideas.detail: The host says Cursor is using GPT-5 as a competitive edge and that switching models is the one advantage the CLI has over Claude Code right now. He does not compare benchmarks; he says GPT-5 claims are not yet verified by his own tests.

key_ideas.idea: The CLI is beta and the host says it carries security risks; install is a copy-paste of a command from Cursor's site, then login through the browser.
key_ideas.detail: Steps: paste the install command, let it run the install script, add the binary to PATH, start with the cursor agent command, then log in in the browser and return to the terminal. The beta warning comes from Cursor itself.

key_ideas.idea: Core context features are missing: no Cursor rules, no ignore files (e.g. .env), no file references, and no image drag and drop.
key_ideas.detail: He calls it a bare-bones agent. Files in the working repo could not be referenced, and images could not be dropped in. The host sees this as the main gap compared with Claude Code's config and context features.

key_ideas.idea: Built-in slash commands are thin: /model works, but new chat and clear do the same thing, and Vim mode exists.
key_ideas.detail: The host praises the model list on the $20 plan: many models, with limits but far cheaper than API use. He notes Claude Code can reach other providers via Claude Code Router, but on API pricing.

key_ideas.idea: A reproducible test prompt: a Kanban app in plain HTML/CSS/JS, a liquid-glass style, and good animations. The first run hung and the same prompt worked on the second try.
key_ideas.detail: The first instance got stuck for about 8 minutes and was cancelled. A new instance with the same prompt created three files. The host admits he does not know why the first run failed.

key_ideas.idea: Visual bugs remained after follow-up, and an image dropped into the project folder was not read.
key_ideas.detail: The header overlapped the board body, and dragging a card made it fill the whole column, losing its shape. A follow-up fixed the card shape but not the overlap. He placed a screenshot in the folder and told the agent about it; the agent seemed to read only the two existing files, so he could not confirm it saw the image.

key_ideas.idea: Verdict: not worth switching yet. He argues the move to terminal removes Cursor's IDE advantage, since many people run Claude Code inside Cursor for its visual layer.
key_ideas.detail: He says the GPT-5 UI output looked good, and he plans to test the same prompt with other tools to tell whether failures come from the agent or the model.

techniques.name: First-run setup for Cursor agent CLI
techniques.how: 1) Copy the install command from Cursor's site (command text not shown in the video). 2) Paste it into the terminal and let the install script run. 3) Add the install directory to PATH (exact path not shown). 4) Start with `cursor agent`. 5) Finish the browser login and return to the terminal. Cursor labels the CLI beta and warns about security risks.
techniques.when: Trying the CLI for the first time, before running anything on a real repo.

techniques.name: Switch models with /model inside the agent
techniques.how: Type the /model slash command inside the running cursor agent session and pick the model, such as GPT-5. The host reports the $20 plan includes many models with usage limits.
techniques.when: Comparing models on the same coding task within one harness without changing tools.

techniques.name: Retry a stalled agent run with the same prompt
techniques.how: If the run shows no progress for several minutes, cancel that instance, start a new one, and send the identical prompt. In the video this worked on the second try. The host says he never found the cause.
techniques.when: The agent hangs with no output. Retry before assuming the prompt or model is at fault.

techniques.name: Fixed-prompt smoke test for a coding agent
techniques.how: Use one prompt with a clear, checkable spec: a single-page Kanban app in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, a named visual style, and an animation requirement. Then check the result by hand: header layout, drag and drop between columns, and whether the card keeps its shape after the drag.
techniques.when: Comparing coding agents or models on UI generation, where visual bugs show up only in use.

techniques.name: Give visual feedback when the CLI cannot take images
techniques.how: Save the screenshot into the project folder and mention its file name in the follow-up prompt. In this test the agent did not appear to read the image, so check whether it used the file before relying on it.
techniques.when: A CLI agent does not support drag-and-drop images and you need it to react to a visual bug.

numbers.claim: Cursor's $20 plan gives access to a wide model list with usage limits. The host says this costs far less than equivalent API usage. This is his estimate, not a measured figure.
First Kanban run hung for about 8 minutes before the host cancelled it. The identical second run finished and created three files.
Test output after follow-up: card-shape bug fixed, header overlap still present.

hot_takes: Moving Cursor to a terminal agent gives up its visual IDE advantage, since many users run Claude Code inside Cursor for that reason.
Cursor's new agent is not worth switching to from Claude Code in its current beta state.
GPT-5's generated Kanban UI looked good, but that is one run with one prompt.
The title's 'Just Launched' framing overstates a beta CLI with thin features; the substance is a single hands-on test.

relevance.why: A coding-agent CLI review with nothing about proxies, budgets, memory, storage or inference.
ProsHarness wraps the Claude Code CLI. This is a rival CLI, and the video says rules files and ignore files are not yet supported, so config parity cannot be assumed.
relevance.action: Keep a Cursor-agent adapter on the watch list. Before any port, check which Claude Code config features (rules, ignore files) it lacks, as noted at [1:17].
